title: Django Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Make a text view
entries.summary: A view is a function that returns a response. path connects the empty path to hello. Open GET /.
notes: Django path patterns do not start with a slash.

entries.name: Send named data
entries.summary: JsonResponse turns a Python dictionary into JSON. Open GET /book/.
notes: Use a dictionary by default; lists need safe=False.

entries.name: Read a checked path number
entries.summary: The int converter turns a matching path part into a Python int. Open GET /double/4/.
notes: A nonmatching converter produces 404 before the view runs.

entries.name: Read a name from the path
entries.summary: The str converter passes one path segment as text. Open GET /hello/Ravi/.
notes: Use text/plain or proper escaping when returning user text.

entries.name: Read a query string
entries.summary: request.GET contains query values. Visit GET /search/?q=cat.
notes: Despite its name, request.GET describes query data, not the entire request.

entries.name: Allow only a chosen method
entries.summary: A view can inspect request.method. A GET request to /check/ is accepted; another method gets 405.
notes: Use 405 for an unsupported method, not 404.

entries.name: Build a URL from its name
entries.summary: reverse finds a route by name and fills its inputs. Open GET /link/.
notes: The keyword name must match the path input name.

entries.name: Send a client elsewhere
entries.summary: redirect creates an HTTP redirect. GET /start/ sends a browser to /hello/.
notes: A redirect causes a second request from the client.

entries.name: Return an error status
entries.summary: The response status describes the result. Open GET /missing/ to see a 404 reply.
notes: Returning error text with status 200 can mislead clients.

entries.name: Return a list safely
entries.summary: JsonResponse normally expects a dictionary. A dictionary can hold a list under a clear key. Open GET /books/.
notes: A named wrapper leaves room for more response information later.

entries.name: Set response metadata
entries.summary: A response object can store headers. GET /note/ has a no-store cache rule.

example.code:
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse, HttpResponseNotAllowed
from django.shortcuts import redirect
from django.urls import path, reverse
import json
def note(request):
    response = HttpResponse("Practice note", content_type="text/plain")
    response["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    return response
urlpatterns = [
path("note/", note),
]

notes: Set headers before returning the response.

entries.name: Make a small health response
entries.summary: A health route gives a small answer that a checker can read. GET /health/ returns one Boolean field.
notes: A simple health response does not prove every outside service is working.
